pathway_name: Prebiotic glutamate synthesis through glyoxylate-pyruvate chemistry and nonenzymatic transamination
scientific_status: Individual reaction stages have experimental support under simulated prebiotic conditions. The complete pathway is a proposed combination of independently studied reactions and has not been demonstrated as a continuous end-to-end synthesis.

molecules.role: Two-carbon building block and reducing agent
Amino acid product before final acid-base equilibration

reactions.name: Geochemical carbon fixation to pyruvic acid
reactions.mechanism: Net reduction and carbon-carbon bond formation promoted by nickel-iron minerals. The equation summarizes the overall transformation rather than specifying individual surface intermediates.
reactions.evidence: Experimentally demonstrated production of pyruvate from carbon dioxide and hydrogen under catalytic conditions.

reactions.name: Imine formation from formaldehyde and ammonia
reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of ammonia to formaldehyde followed by dehydration, represented as the overall imine-forming equilibrium.

conditions.catalyst: None required in the idealized mechanism

reactions.evidence: Mechanistically supported Strecker intermediate; free methanimine is not assumed to accumulate as an isolated stable product.

reactions.name: Cyanide addition to form aminoacetonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Strecker cyanide addition to an imine.

conditions.environment: Aqueous solution containing HCN or cyanide

reactions.evidence: Established Strecker reaction chemistry with prebiotic relevance.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of aminoacetonitrile to glycine
reactions.mechanism: Nitrile hydrolysis through amide intermediates produces glycine.

reactions.name: Nonenzymatic formation of glyoxylate
reactions.mechanism: Formaldehyde-mediated nonenzymatic transamination of glycine. Methylamine is the proposed stoichiometric nitrogen-containing product.
reactions.evidence: Glyoxylate formation experimentally detected. The reaction also generates competing side products, including serine and sarcosine; the displayed equation describes the principal transamination branch.

reactions.name: Aldol addition of pyruvate and glyoxylate
reactions.mechanism: Aldol carbon-carbon bond formation generates maloyl formate, also called 4-hydroxy-2-ketoglutarate.
reactions.yield_context: Maloyl formate observed after 21 hours in a one-pot pyruvate-glyoxylate reaction network.

reactions.name: Dehydration of maloyl formate
reactions.mechanism: Elimination of water creates an alkene, giving fumaroyl formate.
reactions.evidence: Experimentally observed in the prebiotic alpha-ketoacid reaction network.
reactions.yield_context: Fumaroyl formate observed after 21 hours in the complete pyruvate-glyoxylate reaction mixture.

reactions.name: Reduction to alpha-ketoglutarate
reactions.mechanism: Glyoxylate hydrate acts as the reducing agent through a cross-Cannizzaro-type hydride-transfer mechanism. Fumaroyl formate is reduced to alpha-ketoglutarate, while glyoxylate is oxidized to oxalate.
reactions.evidence: Alpha-ketoglutarate formation observed experimentally. An additional route through a double glyoxylate aldol adduct also contributes to its formation.
reactions.yield_context: Approximately 5% alpha-ketoglutarate was detected after 21 hours in the overall pyruvate-glyoxylate reaction mixture; this is not the isolated yield of this individual reduction.

reactions.name: Nonenzymatic transamination to glutamic acid
reactions.mechanism: Glycine transfers its amino group to alpha-ketoglutarate, generating glutamic acid and regenerating glyoxylate.
reactions.evidence: Experimentally demonstrated nonenzymatic production of glutamate.
reactions.yield_context: Reported glutamate yield from glycine and alpha-ketoglutarate under the specified conditions.
reactions.stereochemistry: The product is not established as exclusively L-glutamate.

reactions.name: Acid-base equilibration to glutamate
reactions.mechanism: Deprotonation and redistribution of protons in aqueous solution produces the glutamate monoanion.

pathway_branches.name: Pyruvate formation
pathway_branches.description: Carbon dioxide and hydrogen generate a three-carbon alpha-ketoacid over nickel-iron catalytic surfaces.

pathway_branches.name: Glycine formation
pathway_branches.description: Formaldehyde, ammonia, and hydrogen cyanide undergo Strecker chemistry followed by hydrolysis to produce glycine.

pathway_branches.name: Glyoxylate formation
pathway_branches.description: Glycine reacts with formaldehyde through nonenzymatic transamination, forming glyoxylate.

pathway_branches.name: Five-carbon skeleton construction
pathway_branches.description: Pyruvate and glyoxylate undergo aldol addition, dehydration, and reduction to alpha-ketoglutarate.

pathway_branches.name: Glutamate formation
pathway_branches.description: Glycine transfers its amino group to alpha-ketoglutarate. The resulting glutamic acid equilibrates with glutamate in water.

additional_network_information.stoichiometry_note: All ten displayed reaction equations are balanced for elements and charge. The carbon-fixation reaction is an overall net equation, and some mechanistic intermediates are omitted.
additional_network_information.stereochemical_note: No enantioselective synthesis or enrichment step has been included. The network does not claim selective formation of L-glutamate.
experimental_limitations: The reactions were reported in separate experiments, often with different temperature, pH, pressure, and catalyst requirements.
The presence of multiple products and competing reactions reduces selectivity.
The full sequence starting from only the listed prebiotic feedstocks has not been experimentally established.
The glutamate yield from the complete assembled network cannot be calculated by multiplying the separately reported intermediate yields.
